about.MIT: MIT: short and permissive. Anyone can reuse the code, even in a closed product, by crediting the author.
about.Apache-2.0: Apache 2.0: permissive, with patent protection. A common choice for companies.
about.BSD-3-Clause: BSD 3: permissive like MIT, and forbids using your name to promote a derivative.
about.MPL-2.0: MPL 2.0: modified files stay open; the rest of a product may be closed.
about.GPL-3.0: GPL 3.0: any distributed derivative software must stay open, under the same license.
about.AGPL-3.0: AGPL 3.0: like the GPL, and an online service using it must publish its code too.

license.aboutNone: Without a license, nobody is legally allowed to reuse the code: pick one before welcoming contributors.
